04 · Training & evaluation

One training function, four models

MLP, 1D-CNN, LSTM, and GRU are trained through the same train_model() routine — Adam optimizer, MSE loss, per-epoch validation MAE tracking — so architecture is the only thing that differs between runs. The Random Forest benchmark trains separately with scikit-learn's own .fit().

EPOCHS = 10
LR = 1e-3

def train_model(model, name, train_loader, val_loader, epochs=EPOCHS, lr=LR):
    model.to(device)
    loss_fn = nn.MSELoss()
    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=lr)
    history = {"train_loss": [], "val_loss": [], "val_mae": []}

    for epoch in range(epochs):
        model.train()
        total_loss = 0
        for X_batch, y_batch in train_loader:
            X_batch, y_batch = X_batch.to(device), y_batch.to(device)
            preds = model(X_batch)
            loss = loss_fn(preds, y_batch)
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
            total_loss += loss.item()

        model.eval()
        val_loss, val_preds, val_true = 0, [], []
        with torch.no_grad():
            for X_batch, y_batch in val_loader:
                X_batch, y_batch = X_batch.to(device), y_batch.to(device)
                preds = model(X_batch)
                val_loss += loss_fn(preds, y_batch).item()
                val_preds.extend(preds.cpu().tolist())
                val_true.extend(y_batch.cpu().tolist())

        val_mae = mean_absolute_error(val_true, val_preds)
        history["train_loss"].append(total_loss / len(train_loader))
        history["val_loss"].append(val_loss / len(val_loader))
        history["val_mae"].append(val_mae)

    return history, time.time() - start_time

Held-out test evaluation

After training, every PyTorch model runs once, with gradients disabled, over the official NASA test sequences (each engine's final 30-cycle window). The Random Forest is scored the same way with .predict() on the flattened windows.

evaluate() cell 31 ↗
123456789 
def evaluate(model, X_test, y_test):
    model.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        preds = model(torch.tensor(X_test, dtype=torch.float32).to(device)).cpu().numpy()
    return {
        "MAE": mean_absolute_error(y_test, preds),
        "RMSE": mean_squared_error(y_test, preds) ** 0.5,
        "R2": r2_score(y_test, preds),
    }

Hyperparameters

WINDOW_SIZE 30 cycles Sequence length fed to every model
RUL_CAP 125 cycles Piecewise-linear RUL target cap
BATCH_SIZE 64 DataLoader batching
EPOCHS 10 Training loop
LR 1e-3 Adam optimizer learning rate
